why: Pacing can help you organize activity and recovery around a manageable baseline rather than repeatedly cycling between overdoing and stopping.

slides.title: What Pacing Means
slides.content: Pacing is a flexible planning strategy. It can involve choosing priorities, breaking tasks up, varying demands, and adjusting the dose using your goals and response.

slides.title: There Is No Universal Percentage
slides.content: Fixed rules such as always starting at 50% or increasing by 10% do not fit everyone. Establish a realistic baseline with your clinician when needed.

slides.title: Avoid the Boom-Bust Cycle
slides.content: Doing far more on a good day and then needing prolonged recovery can make routines less predictable. A steadier plan may be easier to build on.

slides.title: Pacing Is Not Permanent Avoidance
slides.content: The aim is meaningful participation. Depending on your plan, capacity can be progressed over time rather than holding activity below the same limit forever.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: Choose one activity, estimate a manageable dose, and note your response during it and later. Use that information to plan the next attempt.
